title: Evil Dead II
tagline: Same cabin, same book, better snacks.
about: Ash takes his girlfriend to a remote cabin, where an old recording wakes the evil in the woods and keeps him trapped there until dawn.
cue: Serve the hand pies when Ash and Linda pull up to the cabin in the opening.
faces: UP THE MOUNTAIN, OVER THE BRIDGE, MIND THE TREES

Knowby CabinEvil Dead IISame cabin, same book, better snacks.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersAsh's runaway hand piesGolden shortcrust pies filled with potato, leek, cheddar and thymeHow to make it3 sheets of frozen shortcrust pastry, thawed400g potatoes, cut into 1cm dice1 leek, thinly sliced20g butter120g cheddar, grated1 tsp thyme leaves1/2 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper1 egg, beatenBoil the diced potato until just tender and drain well.Soften the leek in the butter.Mix the potato, leek, cheddar, thyme, salt and pepper and leave to cool.Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut 8 rounds of 12cm from the pastry, spoon in the filling, fold into half moons, crimp the edges and brush with egg.Bake on a lined tray until deep golden.Jake and Bobbie Joe's hush puppiesCrisp fried cornmeal fritters with spring onion, served with honey butterHow to make it150g fine cornmeal75g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 tsp sugar1/2 tsp salt4 spring onions, finely sliced1 egg180ml buttermilk1 L vegetable oil, for frying60g butter, soft2 tbsp honeyMix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, sugar and salt.Whisk the egg and buttermilk, stir into the dry mix with the spring onion and rest.Beat the butter with the honey.Heat the oil in a deep pot to 180°C.Drop in heaped tablespoons of batter in batches and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden. Drain on paper towel.Serve hot with the honey butter.MainsHenrietta's fruit cellar pork chopsSeared pork chops with apples, onion and sage in a creamy mustard pan sauce, with crushed potatoesHow to make it800g baby potatoes40g butter4 thick pork loin chops1 tsp salt1/2 tsp black pepper1 tbsp vegetable oil2 red apples, cored and cut into wedges1 onion, sliced8 sage leaves250ml chicken stock1 tbsp wholegrain mustard100ml thickened creamBoil the potatoes until tender, drain and crush lightly with a fork and half the butter.Season the chops with the salt and pepper and sear in the oil for 4 minutes a side until just cooked. Rest on a plate.Fry the apples, onion and sage in the rest of the butter until golden.Add 250ml chicken stock and the mustard, bubble to reduce by half, then stir in the cream.Return the chops and their juices to warm through and serve with the potatoes.Annie Knowby's apple-braised chicken with root vegetablesAnnie turns up with the missing pages and a proper dinnerHow to make it1kg chicken thighs, bone in2 onions, in wedges3 carrots, in chunks2 parsnips, in chunks2 apples, in wedges300ml apple juice250ml chicken stock4 sprigs of thyme1 tbsp olive oil1 crusty loafBrown the chicken skin side down in the oil in a heavy pot, then set aside.Add the onion, carrot and parsnip and colour lightly.Add the apple, apple juice, stock and thyme, put the chicken back on top and simmer covered.Uncover and simmer until the sauce reduces. Serve with crusty bread.SweetsKnowby cabin pecan pieShortcrust filled with toasted pecans in a brown sugar and maple custard, with whipped creamHow to make it1 sheet frozen shortcrust pastry, thawed200g pecans3 eggs150g brown sugar125ml maple syrup60g butter, melted1 tsp vanilla extract1/4 tsp salt300ml thickened creamHeat the oven to 180°C. Line a 23cm pie tin with the pastry and chill.Line with baking paper and rice and blind bake, then lift out the paper and rice.Whisk the eggs, brown sugar, maple syrup, butter, vanilla and salt.Scatter the pecans in the pastry case and pour over the filling.Bake until set with a slight wobble in the centre.Cool completely.Whip the cream to soft peaks and serve with slices of pie.DrinksLaughing room peach iced teaBlack tea with fresh peach syrup and lemon over ice, with peach slices and mintHow to make it6 black tea bags1 L boiling water3 ripe peaches, sliced100g caster sugar600ml cold water1 lemon, juiced1 bag ice1 bunch mintSteep the tea bags in the boiling water for 5 minutes and remove.Simmer half the peach slices with the sugar and 100ml of the cold water until soft, then strain to a syrup.Stir the syrup, lemon juice and the rest of the cold water into the tea and chill.Pour over ice with the remaining peach slices and a sprig of mint.
